pairs.prompt: The bridge closed for six months.
pairs.expressing: And what did the town do? It waited. What else could it have done? Nothing, with one road in.
pairs.neutral: The town waited. There was nothing else it could do, with one road in.

pairs.prompt: The harvest failed twice running.
pairs.expressing: Was anyone surprised? Hardly. Had the rains not come late both years? They had.
pairs.neutral: Nobody was surprised. The rains had come late both years.

pairs.prompt: They rewrote the timetable again.
pairs.expressing: Did it help? Not noticeably. Were the trains any fuller? They were not.
pairs.neutral: It did not help noticeably. The trains were no fuller.

pairs.prompt: The lamp burned out on the first night.
pairs.expressing: What are the odds? Better than you would think, on a cheap bulb. Did anyone check the voltage? Nobody had.
pairs.neutral: That is likelier than you would think on a cheap bulb, and nobody had checked the voltage.

pairs.prompt: The committee met for four hours.
pairs.expressing: What came of it? A date for another meeting. Was anything decided? Nothing was.
pairs.neutral: It produced a date for another meeting. Nothing was decided.

pairs.prompt: The river took the lower field.
pairs.expressing: Could it have been stopped? Perhaps, with a bank. Had anyone asked for one? They had, twice.
pairs.neutral: A bank might have stopped it, and people had asked for one twice.

pairs.prompt: The recipe calls for an hour of kneading.
pairs.expressing: Does anyone do that? Almost no one. Does the bread suffer? A little, honestly.
pairs.neutral: Almost nobody does that, and the bread suffers a little.

pairs.prompt: She learned the language in one winter.
pairs.expressing: How? By speaking it badly in public. Is there another way? Not one that works.
pairs.neutral: She did it by speaking it badly in public, which is the only way that works.

pairs.prompt: The old kiln stood unused for years.
pairs.expressing: Why keep it? For the chimney, mostly. Would anyone pay to move it? Nobody would.
pairs.neutral: It was kept mostly for the chimney, and nobody would pay to move it.

pairs.prompt: They planted the orchard on clay.
pairs.expressing: Was that wise? Not really. Did the trees take? Half of them did.
pairs.neutral: That was not wise, and only half the trees took.

pairs.prompt: The ferry runs twice a day in winter.
pairs.expressing: Is that enough? For the island, barely. What happens in a storm? Nothing runs at all.
pairs.neutral: That is barely enough for the island, and in a storm nothing runs at all.

pairs.prompt: He rebuilt the engine from the manual.
pairs.expressing: Did it start? On the third attempt. Had he done it before? Never once.
pairs.neutral: It started on the third attempt, and he had never done it before.

pairs.prompt: The survey went out to four hundred households.
pairs.expressing: How many replied? Sixty. Is that a mandate? It is not.
pairs.neutral: Sixty replied, which is not a mandate.

pairs.prompt: The wall was pointed with cement.
pairs.expressing: What does that do to old stone? It traps the damp. Can it be undone? Slowly, and by hand.
pairs.neutral: That traps the damp in old stone, and undoing it is slow hand work.

pairs.prompt: The choir lost its rehearsal room.
pairs.expressing: Where did they go? The school hall. Was it better? Colder, but larger.
pairs.neutral: They went to the school hall, which was colder but larger.

pairs.prompt: The forecast promised a dry week.
pairs.expressing: And was it? Not after Tuesday. Had anyone brought covers? Only the sensible ones.
pairs.neutral: It was not, after Tuesday, and only the sensible ones had brought covers.

pairs.prompt: They found the ledger in the attic.
pairs.expressing: What was in it? Every wage for thirty years. Who had hidden it? Nobody, it seems.
pairs.neutral: It held every wage for thirty years, and it seems nobody had hidden it.

pairs.prompt: The path floods every spring.
pairs.expressing: Whose job is it? The estate's, in theory. Has anything been done? Not in four years.
pairs.neutral: It is the estate's job in theory, and nothing has been done in four years.

pairs.prompt: The grant covered half the cost.
pairs.expressing: Where did the rest come from? A raffle and a loan. Was that sustainable? Plainly not.
pairs.neutral: The rest came from a raffle and a loan, which was plainly not sustainable.

pairs.prompt: The hens stopped laying in November.
pairs.expressing: Is that normal? Entirely. Does anything help? Light, a little.
pairs.neutral: That is entirely normal, and a little light helps.

pairs.prompt: The lease ran out in March.
pairs.expressing: Did they renew? They did not. What happened to the stock? It went to auction.
pairs.neutral: They did not renew, and the stock went to auction.

pairs.prompt: The museum charges nothing to enter.
pairs.expressing: How does it survive? On a bequest. Will that last? Another decade, perhaps.
pairs.neutral: It survives on a bequest that will perhaps last another decade.

pairs.prompt: He walked the coast in nine days.
pairs.expressing: Alone? Entirely. Would he do it again? He says not.
pairs.neutral: He did it entirely alone and says he would not do it again.

pairs.prompt: The frost came early that year.
pairs.expressing: What did it take? The late beans. Could they have been covered? Easily, had anyone known.
pairs.neutral: It took the late beans, which could easily have been covered had anyone known.

pairs.prompt: The archive digitised its maps.
pairs.expressing: All of them? Only the sheets after 1850. Why stop there? The earlier ones are too fragile.
pairs.neutral: Only the sheets after 1850, because the earlier ones are too fragile.

pairs.prompt: The shop kept the same sign for sixty years.
pairs.expressing: Why change it now? The lettering had gone. Did anyone mind? A few did.
pairs.neutral: It changed because the lettering had gone, and a few people minded.

pairs.prompt: They dug the foundations in August.
pairs.expressing: Was the ground hard? Like brick. Did that slow them? By a fortnight.
pairs.neutral: The ground was like brick, which slowed them by a fortnight.

pairs.prompt: The boat leaked from the first season.
pairs.expressing: Where? Along one seam. Was it ever fixed? Only properly last year.
pairs.neutral: It leaked along one seam and was only properly fixed last year.

pairs.prompt: The library opens on Sunday now.
pairs.expressing: Who asked for that? The students, chiefly. Has it been used? Heavily.
pairs.neutral: The students chiefly asked for it, and it has been heavily used.

pairs.prompt: The hedge was cut to the ground.
pairs.expressing: Will it come back? Thicker than before. How long? Three seasons.
pairs.neutral: It will come back thicker than before, over three seasons.

pairs.prompt: The mill wheel turned again in June.
pairs.expressing: After how long? Forty years. Who paid for it? The village, by subscription.
pairs.neutral: It turned again after forty years, paid for by the village by subscription.

pairs.prompt: The letters were never answered.
pairs.expressing: All of them? Every one. Did anyone follow up? Not until it was far too late.
pairs.neutral: Every one went unanswered, and nobody followed up until it was far too late.
